opportunities.title: APEX Awards
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Established independent researchers with a strong track record and proven ability to lead collaborative work; hold a permanent or fixed-term position covering the duration of the award; have teaching and admin duties from which they can be relieved; based in a UK University or UK not-for-profit research organisation. Lead applicants may include up to two Co-applicants covering a different Academy remit.
opportunities.summary: APEX Awards (Academies Partnership in Supporting Excellence in Cross-disciplinary research), in partnership with the Royal Society and Royal Academy of Engineering and supported by the Leverhulme Trust, offer established independent researchers the opportunity to pursue genuine interdisciplinary and curiosity-driven research to benefit wider society, particularly at the boundary between science, engineering, and the social sciences and humanities.

opportunities.title: SHAPE Involve and Engage
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to any researcher based in the UK who meets the conditions of the call; need not have received British Academy funding previously. Previous successful recipients of this award are not eligible to reapply.
opportunities.summary: Public engagement programme supporting ambitious projects to engage the public with the humanities and social sciences, working in partnership with a gallery, archive, library or museum (GLAM organisation) or a performing arts organisation.

opportunities.title: The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation and The British Academy Knowledge Frontiers Symposium 2027

amount.raw: Symposium covers travel, accommodation and visa costs; seed funding available for collaborations

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early career researchers affiliated with research institutions in the UK or Germany, in the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Invites applications for early career researchers in the humanities and social sciences to attend a research collaboration symposium on the broad theme of 'Humans and Nature: More resilient towards the future', in partnership with The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, taking place 21-23 April 2027.

opportunities.title: Postdoctoral Fellowships

amount.raw: Covered under Full Economic Costing (FEC) regime; Academy funds 80 per cent of salary costs, directly allocated and indirect costs under FEC. Tenable for three years.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Early-career researchers in the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or recognised research organisation. British citizens and EEA nationals eligible regardless of where doctorate obtained; any nationality with a UK doctorate; or strong prior association with UK academic community. Must have completed Viva Voce between 1 April 2024 and 1 April 2027. Not eligible if appointed to a permanent academic post at any time.
opportunities.summary: Three-year award to an annual cohort of outstanding early-career researchers in the humanities or social sciences to pursue an independent research project towards the completion of a significant piece of publishable research, strengthening research and teaching experience and boosting prospects of a permanent academic post.

opportunities.title: Talent Development Awards 2026-27
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicants must be ordinarily resident in the UK, hold a current long-term appointment at a UK-based Higher Education Institution (HEI) or Independent Research Organisation (IRO) for the full duration of the award, and intend to pursue original, independent research within the Humanities or Social Sciences. Independent researchers without institutional affiliation are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Awards promoting the acquisition and advancement of skills in relevant areas by UK-based researchers, supporting innovative research methods through skills development, collaboration or dissemination, in areas such as quantitative skills, data science, digital humanities and languages.

opportunities.title: International Interdisciplinary Research Projects 2027

amount.raw: Up to £300,000 over 2 years (offered at 80% FEC; total project value at 100% FEC may not exceed £375,000)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Principal Investigator must be a researcher from the humanities and social sciences based at an eligible UK university or research institute with an established role lasting at least the duration of the award, postdoctoral or above status, spending at least 20% time (0.2 FTE) on the award. Involvement of overseas Co-Applicants is required.
opportunities.summary: Supports projects engaging with questions concerning the relationship between expertise, public understanding and policy delivery internationally, led by UK-based humanities/social sciences researchers working with international partners on genuinely interdisciplinary projects across SHAPE and STEM disciplines on the theme of Mobilities.

opportunities.title: Global Innovation Fellowships: The German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) 2026-27

amount.raw: Up to £150,000 for 12 months in duration (with Full Economic Costing at 80 per cent)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK-based early- and mid-career researchers from across the humanities and social sciences.
opportunities.summary: Global Innovation Fellowships provide opportunities for UK-based early- and mid-career researchers to develop skills, networks and careers in the creative, cultural, public, private and policy sectors, with award holders embedded in the office of the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) in Berlin, addressing challenges requiring innovative approaches and solutions.

opportunities.title: Additional Needs
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Available to current British Academy award-holders or applicants intending to apply for a British Academy award in the next six months. If not a current award-holder, must identify the scheme they intend to apply for and meet its eligibility requirements.
opportunities.summary: Funding to support additional needs that applicants and award-holders may require, in addition to the amount already requested for research expenses, such as specific equipment to overcome barriers to disabled people undertaking research, assistance for sensory impairment, caring costs, or support in making an application to a British Academy funding call.
